cohort: The study included deliveries by 368,935 women (377,338 infants) from 1999 through 2016.
finding: Pregnant women with endometriosis had significantly higher risks of preterm birth (<37 and <33 weeks) and increased adjusted risks of preeclampsia, placenta previa, postpartum hemorrhage, and small-for-gestational-age status compared to women without endometriosis.
mod_finding: Women in the endometriosis group had more planned cesarean sections (14.0% vs. 8.7%) compared to the unexposed group.
birth_weight: Small-for-gestational-age infants were assessed by birthweight (<10th and <5th percentiles).
gest_age: Preterm birth was defined as <37 and <33 weeks gestational age, and small-for-gestational-age status was also relative to gestational age.
